meta.title: ORA Property Financials Normalized Dataset
meta.noi_definition: revenue (excl. security-deposit receipts and prepaid rent: AppFolio unallocated prepays and Yardi prepaid rental income alike) minus recurring opex
meta.history_note: history[entity]: monthly(bool), yr[year] and ytd[year] (Jan-Sep) with br, rev, opex, noi, cats{opex category}, rc{revenue category}, n months; months{g,br,rv,ox,tx} monthly series; ev[] net base-rent steps; drv[period] account-level drivers with nature (recurring|lumpy|mixed|annual). Years with n<12 are partial.

portfolio.note: Same-store excludes lease-up and partial-history assets (9620 State 350, 3034 Westerville, 3875-3883 Livingston). FY view adds the two entity-level statements (55 New Plant, 1851 South Club Solar). TTM/YTD views use PM monthly exports only.

insights.title: Solar electricity income fell 55% in 2025
insights.finding: Total energy income fell -15.7% ($409,839 to $345,537). Electricity sales dropped from $132.5K to $59.3K while SREC income rose from $277.4K to $286.2K. Operating NOI fell $75.6K and Maryland entity tax is a separate $33.8K.
insights.action: Get monthly production, meter reads and the power-sale billing statements for 2024-2026. Confirm there is no curtailment, meter fault or counterparty billing gap. Review SREC sale timing and pricing.
insights.impact_basis: FY25 vs FY24 energy income [ACTUAL YoY]

insights.title: FVC base rent run-rate is falling
insights.finding: Q3 2026 annualized base rent is $0.64M versus $0.70M in Q3 2025 (-8.0%), after +5.5% the year before. YTD 2026 base rent is -1.0% against Jan-Sep 2025. FVC is the largest rent line in the folder (about 26% of trailing base rent) and carries almost no expense recoveries.
insights.action: Pull the FVC rent roll by unit for Jun-Sep 2026 and separate vacancy, concessions and rent cuts. Get a property-level P&L split (the file is an all-properties aggregate). Set a leasing target for the vacated space and review every renewal for a mark-to-market.
insights.impact_basis: Q3-26 vs Q3-25 annualized base rent [ESTIMATE]

insights.title: Livingston re-leased about 45% below the prior rent, and Aug-Sep base rent shows $0
insights.finding: Base rent was $9,192/mo from Oct 2025 to Jun 2026. The new lease (tenant 072 llc, 10,950 SF, executed 02/2026) is $5,032.62/mo ($5.52/SF NNN) with 3% annual steps and a $1,677.54/mo tax/insurance/CAM estimate. Base rent starts 09/01/2026 per the lease, yet the PM exports show $5,032.62 in Jul 2026 and $0 in Aug and Sep 2026. All-in new rent is about $6,710/mo ($7.32/SF with the estimate) against $9,192/mo before.
insights.action: Confirm whether September rent was billed and collected and whether the July receipt was the first month paid at signing. Confirm what the $9,192 covered (gross vs NNN, one or both buildings). If the roll-down is real, decide whether to push the 3% step schedule or the NNN estimate true-up harder.
insights.impact_basis: Prior $9,192/mo vs new $5,032.62/mo base rent x 12 [ESTIMATE; depends on whether prior rent was gross]

insights.title: Broadway water and sewer doubled year over year
insights.finding: Water and Sewer is $38.6K for Jan-Sep 2026 against $18.7K in 2025 (+107.0%), and $46.6K in FY2024 versus $21.4K in FY2025. Annualized 2026 is about $51.4K. Utility reimbursements rose +59.6% to $24.7K, so net unrecovered utilities are up about $13.4K.
insights.action: Pull the utility invoices and meter reads. Check for a leak or irrigation fault, a rate or sewer-surcharge change, estimated-read billing, and a stuck meter. Question the swing between years with the city. Add leak detection and submeters if tenants are billed.

insights.title: Red Branch repairs tripled and snow rose 55%
insights.finding: Repairs and maintenance are $24.5K YTD against $8.0K (+206%): roof repair $8.9K (was $1.7K) and HVAC repair $5.5K (was $0.4K). Snow removal is $14.6K versus $9.4K. FY2025 electricity was $23.3K versus $12.3K (+91%) and gas $6.7K versus $2.8K.
insights.action: Get a roof condition report and a replace-versus-repair comparison before more repair spend. Rebid the snow contract (include a per-push and seasonal-cap option). Price a competitive electricity and gas supply contract for the common-area meters.
insights.impact_basis: YTD26 vs YTD25 R&M plus grounds/snow increase [ACTUAL, 9 months]

insights.title: Red Branch lost $34.9K of base rent to vacancy, waivers and bad debt in 2025
insights.finding: Contra-revenue was $34.9K in FY2025 (5.7% of base rent): vacancy $20.9K, commercial waivers $9.2K and bad debt $4.9K (prepaid rent is excluded from revenue since 2026-10-06). It is $20.7K TTM through Sep 2026. Info Lane contra-revenue is rising too ($8.2K TTM, 1.4% to 2.1% of rent).
insights.action: Get the vacancy by suite and the waiver and bad-debt schedule by tenant. Tie each waiver to a signed concession. Tighten collections on the $4.9K bad-debt tenants and put the vacant suites on a leasing clock.
insights.impact_basis: TTM contra-revenue at Red Branch [UPPER BOUND of what is recoverable]

insights.title: FVC and Rarig carry almost all operating cost themselves
insights.finding: Reimbursements cover 4% of the recoverable pool at FVC and 10% at Rarig, against 103% at Red Branch and 132% at 3540 E 5th. FVC's FY2025 pool (tax, insurance, utilities, grounds, repairs) was $164.5K, about 23% of revenue.
insights.action: At every renewal and new lease, move gross leases to NNN or modified gross with a base-year stop. Bill utilities by submeter or ratio. Confirm which FVC and Rarig leases already allow pass-throughs and are not being billed.
insights.impact_basis: Each +10 points of recovery on the FVC pool [SENSITIVITY]

insights.title: Real estate tax is the largest cost line; run an appeal program
insights.finding: FY2025 real estate and property tax across the nine PM properties is $328.6K (35% of operating expense). Same-store tax grew +4.3% in FY2025. Info Lane is +20% YTD and Red Branch +13% in FY2025.
insights.action: Run the tax-appeal workflow on every property with a year-over-year increase above 5% before each county deadline. Track bill versus appeal outcome in the dashboard. Prioritize Info Lane, Red Branch, Rarig and Broadway.

insights.title: 9620 recovers about 15% of its recoverable cost
insights.finding: TTM recoverable pool is $69.9K (tax, insurance, utilities, grounds, repairs) against $10.8K billed (CAM estimates $5.0K and reconciliation $5.8K). Base rent has grown from about $6.7K/mo to $15.3K/mo in 12 months as the building leases up.
insights.action: Audit each lease for CAM, tax and insurance obligations. Move CAM billing to monthly estimates sized to budget, then run a year-end reconciliation. Confirm vacant-space cost is not being swallowed.
insights.impact_basis: Each +10 points of recovery on the 9620 pool [SENSITIVITY]

insights.title: FVC utilities are up 70% YTD; taxes are down 60% (verify)
insights.finding: Utilities are $23.0K YTD against $13.5K: meter reader $3.4K (was $0.7K), electricity +73%, gas +167%, water +34%, plus a $4.3K water line repair and $1.6K water meter installation. Reimbursements for utilities are up to $10.9K from $5.8K. Real estate tax is $16.8K YTD against $42.0K.
insights.action: Confirm whether the tax drop is a successful appeal or a missing installment (cash basis). If the second-half bill is unpaid, accrue it. Continue the water submeter program and bill tenants the same month. Rebid electricity supply.
insights.impact_basis: Increase in net unrecovered utilities YTD [ACTUAL, 9 months]

insights.title: Management fees run about 4% of revenue; two properties are above
insights.finding: Total TTM management fees across the nine PM-reported properties are $117.3K (3.8% of revenue). 9620 State 350 is 5.0% and Livingston is 4.0%. The 3540 E 5th lease caps the recoverable fee at 3% of rent plus adjustment rent.
insights.action: Bid the management contract across the portfolio or move to a tiered fee (lower rate above a revenue threshold). Make sure the fee base excludes security deposits and prepaid items.
insights.impact_basis: Each 50 bps of fee on trailing revenue [SENSITIVITY]

insights.title: Bid out snow, landscaping and trash contracts as a package
insights.finding: Grounds, snow and lot cost is $80.4K TTM across the nine properties. Same-store snow/grounds were -5% in FY2025 but individual contracts moved sharply: Red Branch snow +55% YTD, Info Lane snow $4.5K to $14.6K in FY2025, Broadway snow contract +53% in FY2025. Broadway also pays $13.8K for contract cleaning and $3.6K for an elevator contract.
insights.action: Issue one RFP per metro (Columbus and Maryland) for snow, landscaping, trash and janitorial. Require unit pricing and seasonal caps. Rebid every 24-36 months and compare invoices to push counts.

insights.title: 3540 E 5th recoveries exceed the property-level reimbursable cost
insights.finding: TTM recoveries were $29.0K versus total property operating cost of $23.1K. The lease (AR Tenant 012 / Syn201 of Syn405, REDACTED-AMT SF, 04/2023 to 07/2033) is NNN with 2.5% annual steps ($14,801.15/mo from Aug 2026) and a 3% management-fee cap on rent plus adjustment rent. Rent is on schedule. The gap suggests recoveries include prior-year true-ups or a capital pass-through.
insights.action: Run the CAM/tax/insurance reconciliation for the last two lease years and confirm what is in the reimbursement. If capital is being amortized to the tenant, document it. If it is an over-bill, correct it before the tenant audits.
insights.impact_basis: TTM recoveries minus total opex [ESTIMATE of possible over-recovery]

insights.title: Broadway rent grows about 2% a year, with steady waivers
insights.finding: Base rent run-rate: +2.0% in 2025 and +2.0% in 2026 (about $24.6K to $25.5K/mo in small steps). Commercial rental waivers run 2.9% of base rent ($8.8K TTM; prepaid rent is excluded from revenue since 2026-10-06).
insights.action: Audit each lease escalator against what is billed. If standard bumps are 3% or fixed steps, Broadway is under-billing. Ask for a waiver log with reasons and end dates.
insights.impact_basis: Each +1 point of annual rent growth [SENSITIVITY]

insights.title: 9620: insurance +55% TTM, an unexplained $6.2K expense, and a 5% management fee
insights.finding: Insurance is $31.6K TTM against $20.4K. A $6,169 miscellaneous expense posted in 2026 YTD. Management fee is 5.0% of revenue against 4.0% at most other properties, and real estate tax shows a $4,034 credit in 2026.
insights.action: Remarket the insurance policy with the portfolio. Get the invoice behind the $6,169. Renegotiate the fee to a flat 4% of collected revenue. Confirm the tax credit and the CAM property-tax recovery.
insights.impact_basis: 25% of the premium increase through a rebid [SPECULATIVE]

insights.title: Info Lane: HVAC repairs, a new association fee and a 20% tax increase
insights.finding: Non-recurring HVAC repairs are $9.9K YTD, an association fee of $3.7K appears for the first time, and real estate taxes are $26.2K versus $21.8K (+20%). FY2025 also carried a $25.5K suite cleaning and preparation charge (vacancy turnover) and snow of $14.6K versus $4.5K.
insights.action: File a property tax appeal. Ask the manager why an association fee started and whether it is recoverable. Replace-versus-repair review on the HVAC units. Get a turnover cost budget per suite.

insights.title: Rarig real estate tax doubled YTD
insights.finding: Taxes are $18.6K Jan-Sep 2026 against $8.7K (+114%), while FY2025 was $17.6K against $26.5K in FY2024. Cash timing may explain part. Legal fees were $3.7K in FY2025 and accounting $2.1K new in 2026.
insights.action: Compare the actual tax bills for the last three tax years to the amounts paid. Appeal if the new valuation outpaces rent.

insights.title: Westerville 45% step-up is captured; verify the May receipt
insights.finding: Scheduled rent stepped from $5,484.87 to $7,969.46 on 04/01/2026 (18,360 SF, Tenant 069 LLC, expires 09/30/2030). TTM NOI is $83.0K against $11.8K the prior year. May 2026 shows $10,147 received, $2,177 above schedule. The lease's $1,875/mo tax and insurance estimate tracks actual cost (taxes plus insurance TTM $22.4K against $22.5K estimated).
insights.action: Confirm what the extra $2,177 in May represents (catch-up, true-up or a posting error). Calendar the 3.5% step each April through 2030.

insights.title: Fishel: no rent bumps for 5 years, renewal rent already fixed at +2%
insights.finding: Tenant 077 LLC (24,000 SF) paid a flat $5,233/mo ($2.62/SF/yr) for the full 60-month term ending 09/30/2026. The renewal option was exercised for 10/01/2026 at $5,337.98/mo, with 2% annual steps to $5,778.00 in year 5. The lease fixes the renewal rent, so there is no market reset. No P&L for this address is in the folder (it may sit inside FVC).
insights.action: Treat this as a lease-form lesson: renewal options should be at the greater of fixed or fair market value (the Sunburst lease uses that structure) and initial terms should carry 3% steps. Each $0.61/SF on 24,000 SF is $14,707/yr.

insights.title: 55 New Plant rent matches the lease; lease ends 12/31/2027; entity cash is earning interest
insights.finding: Tenant 143 LLC (34,534 SF, Owings Mills MD) rent is $21,162 in year 1 with 3% annual steps: $21,797 (2024), $22,451 (2025), $23,125 (2026), $23,818 (2027). FY2025 rent of $270,089 and 2026 YTD of $115,624 (exactly five payments) both tie to the schedule. Interest expense fell from $20.0K (2025) to $2.0K (2026 YTD) while interest income was $48.0K YTD, which points to a debt payoff and a large cash balance in the entity.
insights.action: Start the renewal or backfill plan now: the term ends 12/31/2027 and the renewal clause was not fully read (OCR of the scan was partial). Put idle entity cash to work against the $429-800M growth plan.

insights.title: Insurance is flat once cash timing is removed; rebid it as one program
insights.finding: On the six same-store PM properties (complete in every window), FY2025 insurance is +30.2% against FY2024 but TTM26 is -1.8% against TTM25. The difference is cash timing (Info Lane shows $0 in FY2024). Livingston (3 of 12 months in TTM25), Westerville (11 of 12) and 9620 State 350 (lease-up; TTM $20.4K to $31.6K) are outside the comparison. TTM premiums across all nine PM properties are $101.6K.
insights.action: Rebid the property and liability program on a blanket basis ahead of renewals. Add a renewal calendar to the dashboard so premium timing is visible.

data_quality: All statements are cash basis. Real estate tax, insurance and snow are lumpy by payment date, so year-over-year category moves in a single period can be timing. Prefer FY and TTM views for tax and insurance.
The consolidated 2026 YTD P&Ls in the folder end around 2026-06-12 (three are labeled 12/31/26). The monthly PM exports run through 2026-09-30 and are the basis for all 2026 numbers here.

Monthly data reconciles to the annual P&Ls to the dollar for Rarig, Broadway, Info Lane, 3540 E 5th, Red Branch and FVC (FY2024, FY2025). Livingston FY2025 differs by $2.1K of opex (July 2025 export missing). 9620 FY2025 revenue now ties to the annual file ($113,408); the $4.0K gap (monthly $117,414) came from the single-month 2025-09 recap, whose expense lines were read as revenue, and was corrected on 2026-10-05. 9620 FY2025 opex ties except management fees, $0.77K above the annual file (monthly $8,824 against $8,058).
FVC is an all-properties aggregate (Sepich portfolio). Property-level and unit-level results are not available from the files.
Missing monthly exports: Westerville 2024-01 to 2024-08 and 2024-10; Livingston 2024-01 to 2025-05 and 2025-07; 9620 2024-01 to 2024-08 (pre-ownership).
55 New Plant (EGFLLC) and 1851 South Club Solar are entity-level annual QuickBooks statements with no monthly detail. Their 2026 figures end about 2026-06-12.

NOI here is normalized: revenue less recurring operating cost. Capital items, leasing commissions, tenant improvements, owner distributions, debt service, interest, depreciation and entity income tax are excluded. Security deposit receipts and prepaid rent are excluded from revenue, with one treatment for every statement layout: AppFolio unallocated prepays and the Yardi cash-flow Prepaid Rental Income line (Broadway, Red Branch) are both excluded (ruling 2026-10-06; until then the Yardi line was counted as contra-revenue). PM-reported NOI differs: for example FVC reported NOI nets $37.0K of owner distributions and $7.2K of replacements in FY2025.
2203-2207 Northwood is excluded as instructed. Its P&Ls are in the folder but were not used.
Square footage, lease expiration dates and tenant rolls are not in the P&L files. $/SF metrics need the Master Workbook or Notion tenant data. Only the six leases above provide SF.
The Sepich all-properties HTML export (2015 to 2026-09-30) was not used. It is one cumulative period.
Owner distribution and contribution signs differ between PM report layouts. Treat the dist field as net owner cash out as reported, not as a control total.
